--- title: "[FittedRecipe.transform()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Apply each fitted step in order, skipping ``RowOp`` and identity steps. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/tidymodels/shoez/blob/examples-section/shoez/recipe.py#L589-L642){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python FittedRecipe.transform(data) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ``RowOp`` steps never run on new data; steps whose primary selection resolved to zero columns at fit time (``_empty_selection``) are the identity transform and pass the frame through unchanged. Both are skipped here — structurally, by inspecting the step rather than by any per-step convention. Never re-estimates. Returns a native frame at the sklearn boundary. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ``transform()`` applies the fitted statistics to new data, returning a native frame with the same schema the recipe learned at fit time: ::: {#69e8f8e6 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df = pd.DataFrame( {"age": [25, 41, 33, 52], "city": ["NYC", "LA", "NYC", "SF"]} ) fitted = ( Recipe() .add(StepNormalize(s.numeric_predictors())) .add(StepDummy(s.nominal_predictors())) .fit(df) ) fitted.transform(df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
age city_NYC city_SF
0 -1.105912 1 0
1 0.281899 0 0
2 -0.412006 1 0
3 1.236019 0 1
``` ::: :::
